[Charts & Diagrams] Q: In a Venn diagram, set A has 20 elements, set B has 15 elements, and A ∩ B has 8 elements. How many elements are in A ∪ B?
[Common Calculation Pitfalls] Q: A student calculates the mean of grouped data as 45.2 using class upper bounds instead of midpoints. The classes are 10–20, 20–30, 30–40. What should they have used?
questions.correctAnswer: Midpoints: 15, 25, 35. Using upper bounds (20, 30, 40) overestimates each value by 5, shifting the mean upward.
questions.explanation: Midpoints: 15, 25, 35. Using upper bounds (20, 30, 40) overestimates each value by 5, shifting the mean upward.

questions.question: [Common Calculation Pitfalls] Q: A student computes P(A or B) = 0.6 + 0.7 = 1.3. Why is this wrong?
questions.correctAnswer: A probability cannot exceed 1. The events are not mutually exclusive, so P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B). The overlap must be subtracted.
questions.explanation: A probability cannot exceed 1. The events are not mutually exclusive, so P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B). The overlap must be subtracted.

questions.question: [Common Calculation Pitfalls] Q: Calculate the percentage change when a value rises from 80 to 100. A student writes (100÷80) × 100 = 125%. Is this correct?
questions.correctAnswer: The student found 125% of the original, not the percentage change. Percentage change = ((100−80)/80) × 100 = (20/80) × 100 = 25% increase.
questions.explanation: The student found 125% of the original, not the percentage change. Percentage change = ((100−80)/80) × 100 = (20/80) × 100 = 25% increase.

questions.question: [Correlation & Regression] Q: Two judges rank 5 contestants. The rank differences are: 0, 1, 1, 2, 0. Calculate Spearman's rₛ.
[Correlation & Regression] Q: Pearson's r for two variables is –0.85. Describe the correlation.
questions.correctAnswer: Strong negative linear correlation: as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease, and the points lie close to a straight line with negative slope.
questions.explanation: Strong negative linear correlation: as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease, and the points lie close to a straight line with negative slope.

questions.question: [Correlation & Regression] Q: A line of best fit is drawn for data where x ranges from 10 to 50. Is predicting y when x = 30 interpolation or extrapolation?
questions.correctAnswer: Interpolation, because x = 30 is within the observed range of 10 to 50.
questions.explanation: Interpolation, because x = 30 is within the observed range of 10 to 50.

questions.question: [Data Cleaning & Reliability] Q: What is data cleaning?
questions.correctAnswer: The process of checking a data set for errors, missing values and anomalies and correcting or removing them before analysis.
questions.explanation: The process of checking a data set for errors, missing values and anomalies and correcting or removing them before analysis.

questions.question: [Data Cleaning & Reliability] Q: How should you deal with an outlier?
questions.correctAnswer: Investigate it: if it is a data entry error, correct or remove it; if it is genuine, keep it but note its effect on results.
questions.explanation: Investigate it: if it is a data entry error, correct or remove it; if it is genuine, keep it but note its effect on results.

questions.question: [Data Cleaning & Reliability] Q: What is the difference between reliability and validity?
questions.correctAnswer: Reliability means consistency (getting the same result on repetition); validity means the method measures what it is supposed to measure.
questions.explanation: Reliability means consistency (getting the same result on repetition); validity means the method measures what it is supposed to measure.
